english: A bear came to the village and was stealing the sheep. The people trembled. A shepherd carrying a bow went to the rock (or: to the ford). He caught sight of the bear and killed it. The people gave him a famous name, 'Bear-slayer'. He had great fame. His fame is imperishable.
uncertain: pérwr̥: lexicon has two homographs, 'ford, crossing' and 'rock; mountain'; either fits as goal of gʷéh₂t
ḱóymom: read as ḱóymos-2 'village, home' (ACC of goal); also adjective 'homely, belonging to the family'
h₂r̥tḱogʷʰonóm: not analyzed; read as compound h₂ŕ̥tḱos + gʷʰonós 'striker' = 'bear-slayer', apposition to h₁nómn̥
h₁ést: read as PST 'was' (h₁ésti); could formally be AOR of h₁est 'shot'
moréyet: PST (ongoing) used for the killing; translated as completed

english: Dogs, listen sharply and follow the path. Now do not run forward into the river. May the wolf not look at you.
uncertain: h₂ḱh₂owsyéte: PRS/PST/IMP 2PL ambiguous; IMP chosen (charm addresses dogs)
sékʷedʰwe: MID PRS/IMP 2PL; IMP chosen
déh₂nu pró: river as ACC goal with pró 'forward'; could be LOC 'in the river'
usmé: 2PL ACC 'you (pl.)'; analyzer also offers a PST.1PL of an unglossed westi-2, rejected

english: The bear was lying in its bed in winter. A dog found the bear's bed and made noise. The daughter heard it, and she came with her father. The bear woke up. She threw a spear, and it pierced the bear's knee. The bear fled to the rock (or: to the ford). The father said: 'It will die.'
uncertain: str̥h₃méni: LOC 'in the bed' with no possessive; 'its' supplied
h₁ím: masc ACC, taken to refer to the dog (ḱwṓ) rather than the bear
pérwr̥: 'rock/mountain' vs 'ford' homographs
bʰéwgt: 'fled' (bhewgt-3) vs 'brought benefit' (bhewgt-4); 'fled' fits
méreti: SBJV 3SG 'will die / let it die'

english: Daughter, sit down. Take the wool. Join it (twist it together) and work. Make a garment for your sister. If you make the garment, you will not get cold in winter.
uncertain: yungdʰí: 'join' — presumably spinning/twisting the wool
wr̥ǵdʰí / wérǵesi: wergjt homographs 'enclose / work, make / shear'; 'make' fits
pĺ̥h₂seh₂m: 'a type of women's garment' (unspecific)
h₁yód: relative neuter used as 'if/when'

english: The carpenter was building a dwelling for the lord. He was setting it up. The dwelling was big. The lord entered it and sat down in it.
uncertain: h₁ésmi: read as LOC.SG anaphoric 'in it'; formally also 'I am' (PRS.1SG), which does not fit
h₁ést: 'was' vs AOR 'shot'; 'was' fits
wiḱpótis: NOM/GEN/ABL ambiguous; NOM as subject of wéyḱt

english: The man threw his own spear, and it broke. The wolf ran at him. The man became afraid. His brother seized a javelin. The javelin pierced its (the wolf's) heart. The wolf died. Then the brother made a spear for the man.
uncertain: Hrumptó: analyzed MID.PST 3SG 'was breaking'; translated as 'broke'
h₁ésyo ḱḗr: 'its heart' taken as the wolf's (masc GEN fits wolf or man; context favors wolf)
wérǵt: 'made' (wergjt-2) vs 'enclosed'/'sheared'

english: The shepherd gave wool to the smith. The smith gave an awl to the carpenter. The carpenter handed a wheel (or: cart) to the shepherd. He who gives, receives.
uncertain: kʷékʷlom: 'wheel; circle; cart; wagon; chariot' — sense unclear
h₁áyto: MID AOR 'received' vs active h₁áyt 'gave'; gnomic sense

english: Net, seize the beast, hold it fast. Let nothing escape from you, and may the net be filled.
uncertain: kapyé: IMP of a present 'to be grasping' — 'keep hold of it'
kʷid mē: unaccented indefinite + mē = 'may nothing'
bʰugyéh₁t: 'flee/escape' (bhewgt-3) vs 'bring benefit' (bhewgt-4)

english: The dogs were driving the beast to the river. It swam in the water. They did not swim (or: they did not catch it). It came out on the other side. It was looking at them. A stranger drew a bow and let fly. It escaped. The stranger had no great fame.
uncertain: sn̥h₂ént: ambiguous — AOR 3PL of sénh₂t 'catch' ('they did not catch [it]') or PST 3PL of snéh₂ti 'swim' ('they did not swim')
h₁éy: masc NOM.SG 'it' (the beast); NOM.PL also possible but verbs are 3SG
h₂éǵont: PST 3PL vs participle; finite PST chosen
gʰóstis: 'guest / stranger / enemy'
déwkt: PST 'was drawing'; translated 'drew'
h₁ést: 'was' vs AOR 'shot'

english: Dawn, shine, show us the path. May the beast come to us. Then may we see it.
uncertain: ǵʰwḗr-ge n̥smé gʷm̥yóyh₁t: positive wish 'may the beast come to us' (no mē); read as a hunting prayer. If a protective prayer was meant, mē is missing
nos: enclitic ACC/GEN/DAT 1PL; DAT 'to us' with déyḱe
n̥smé: 1PL ACC as goal 'to us'; analyzer also offers AOR.1PL of nest, rejected

english: The smith was fashioning (of?) a spear. He gave it a famous name, 'Wolf-slayer'. The spear slew a wolf. Its name became famous. It has great fame.
uncertain: gʷréws: GEN/ABL of gʷéru; object of tḗtḱt expected in ACC (gʷéru)
h₁ésmey: m/n DAT; taken as the spear (neuter), not the smith
wl̥kʷogʷʰonóm: unanalyzed; read as wĺ̥kʷos + gʷʰonós 'wolf-slayer'
gʷéru: NOM/ACC; read as subject 'the spear slew'; as instrument INS would be expected
gʷʰént: PST 'was slaying'; translated 'slew'
misfit: gʷréws: GEN/ABL.SG 'of a spear' where tḗtḱt needs an ACC object (gʷéru)

english: Mist lay on the field. The daughter was stretching a net between the stones. She sat down. A piglet came out of the mist and went into it (the net). She stood up and killed it with a stone. She cried out, and her mother heard her voice. The mother came, and the daughter rejoiced. The two of them took it home.
uncertain: h₃mígʰleh₂: analyzer gives only VOC.SG (lexicon entry has no gender; other eh₂-stems like h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ get NOM.SG); read as NOM subject of ḱéyto — lexicon gap, not a text error
h₁ím (after wéyḱt): masc ACC, taken as the net (tn̥tlós m)
HréwdHt: 3SG with no stated subject; taken as the daughter (her voice is heard next); could be the piglet
duktā́m: PST/IMP 3DU 'the two were leading/dragging'; zero-grade stem differs from déwkt in other items
ḱóymom: 'home' (ACC of goal)

english: The twins were climbing to the rock (mountain) with the dog. It saw a wolf, and we followed it. The wolf was swift and vanished. The twins sat down and were thirsty. The two said: 'The wolf is swift and the mountain is high. Let us go home. At dawn we will come again.'
uncertain: h₁éy: masc NOM.SG, taken as the dog; kʷéḱt is 3SG
sékʷomedʰh₂: MID PST 1PL 'we were following' in a 3rd-person dual narrative
h₁éyomes / gʷm̥yṓmes: SBJV 1PL spoken by two twins; dual would be expected unless inclusive
pérwr̥: rock/mountain vs ford; 'great' in later line favors mountain
h₂ew: 'again' vs 'away'
misfit: sékʷomedʰh₂: 1PL 'we followed' in a 3rd-person narrative whose subjects are the dual twins (expected 3DU)

english: The sheep said to the horses: 'My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses.'
uncertain: whole text: written in Schleicher's 1868 notation (awis, akwabʰyams, wawakat, agʰnutai), not the corpus notation; nothing is analyzable; translated from knowledge of Schleicher's fable
misfit: whole text: Schleicher-style notation, incompatible with the corpus laryngeal/accent notation; no form analyzes

english: Give bones to the dog. Lead it to water and let it drink. Do not hit it. Whoever hits it, it does not follow that one. It is dear.
uncertain: wódr̥: ACC as goal 'to water'; 'bring it water' would need DAT for h₁ím
wédʰe: 'lead' vs 'bring' (wedheti) vs 'bind, marry' (wedheti-2)
stunéds: PST 2SG injunctive with mē = prohibitive
sékʷetor: MID PRS 3SG 'follows' vs SBJV of sekwt-2/-3

english: The god Werunos went down from the sky.
uncertain: wérunos: not in lexicon; taken as a divine name (Varuna)
km̥tá: not in lexicon; taken as 'down'
gʷah₂t: analyzer accepts it as gʷéh₂t AOR 3SG 'went', but it is written with a-vowel and no accent (older notation mixed with laryngeals)
misfit: gʷah₂t: notation flag only (grammatically fits): old-style a-vocalism and no accent, corpus form is gʷéh₂t

english: The horses said: 'Listen, sheep! Our hearts pain us, seeing this: man, the master, makes the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep has no wool.'
uncertain: whole text: Schleicher's 1868 notation; nothing is analyzable; translated from knowledge of Schleicher's fable
wiwidwant- swas: in Schleicher this is one compound 'vividvant-svas' ('us seeing'); split here by a space, so 'swas' was mis-analyzed as swos ACC.PL
misfit: whole text: Schleicher-style notation, incompatible with the corpus notation
wiwidwant- swas: hyphenated compound broken into two tokens

english: The man found a stone (in the) field. He split it and made a quern from it. He was carrying the quern home. His wife saw it and rejoiced.
uncertain: h₂éǵrom: ACC.SG; 'in the field' would be LOC h₂éǵroy; as ACC it is a second object or a goal
h₂éḱmonm̥: 'stone' (vs 'heaven')
h₁ím (last sentence): masc ACC, taken as the quern (gʷréh₂wō m)
misfit: h₂éǵrom: ACC beside the object h₂éḱmonm̥ where LOC h₂éǵroy 'in the field' is expected

english: What have you seen, son? 'I have seen the bear's track.' Follow it. Do not go to the river at night. Listen to the dog. It hears sharply. When it barks, stand still. Do not flee from the bear. Hold up the spear.
uncertain: stóygʰom: 'path, way' — read as the bear's trail
HréwdHeti: 'cries (vocally)'; for a dog, 'barks/howls'
sth₂dʰí: 'stand up'; 'stand firm/still' in context
h₁éy: masc NOM.SG 'it', the dog

english: God, giver of good things, may the guest eat. Now may the lady of the house eat; may we be satisfied.
uncertain: h₁uséwōm: GEN.PL of 'good' used substantively, 'of good things'
gʰóstis: 'guest' vs 'stranger, enemy'; 'guest' fits
tr̥pih₁mé: 'be sated' (terpt-2) vs 'turn' (trept-2); 'be sated' fits
pótnih₂: 'mistress; wife'

english: Perkunos slew the serpent. Wolf, go away from the field; do not come to the sheep. May the javelin strike you; may the spear strike you.
uncertain: gʷʰént: PST 'was slaying'; translated 'slew' (mythic precedent)
litdʰí: 'go away' (leytt) vs 'touch' (leytt-2)
gʷm̥yés: PST 2SG injunctive with mē = prohibitive
twé: 2SG ACC 'you' (not possessive VOC)

english: The man cut down an oak. He carved a bow out of it. He took sinew and stretched it on the bow. He drew the bow. He gave the bow to his brother.
uncertain: dʰn̥wéni: LOC 'on the bow'
déwkt: PST 'was drawing'; translated 'drew'

english: Find an oak. Cut it down. Carve a wheel from it. Bore it through with an awl. If the wheel breaks, do not cry. Make the wheel again. He who does not break (give up) is dear to his mother.
uncertain: h₂isḱé: 'seek, search for'
h₁óloh₁: INS.SG 'with an awl' vs NOM/ACC dual
HréwdHs: PST 2SG injunctive with mē = prohibitive
Hrumptór: MID PRS 3SG 'breaks' — applied to a person, figurative 'gives up/breaks down'
h₂ew: 'again' vs 'off'

english: Wheel, run! Wheel, do not break! May the two horses be swift. Then may the shepherd's heart rejoice.
uncertain: h₁sih₁tā́m: OPT 3DU of 'be' (vs 'throw, shoot')
Hrumpth₂é: MID PST 2SG with mē = prohibitive

english: Perkunos, hear our word. Give us swift dogs. May my spear not go astray. May the beast not escape from us. May we bring meat home. Then we shall give the heart to you.
uncertain: nos: enclitic GEN 'our' (first) and DAT 'to us' (second)
méne: 1SG GEN 'my' (not IMP of meneti)
h₃slidʰyéh₁t: 'slip, go astray' (miss)
wédʰoyh₁me: 'bring' vs 'marry'
déh₃omes: SBJV 1PL 'we shall give'

english: Take wool and join (twist) it. Make a net out of it. Stretch it between the stones. Sit down and do not cry out. When the beast enters the net, stand up and strike it. Whoever sits and does not cry out, to him the beast comes.
uncertain: h₁ésyeh₂s: fem GEN/ABL; ABL 'out of it' (the wool)
tétḱdʰi: IMP of tḗtḱti 'create'; accent written on first syllable, unlike other -dʰí imperatives
HréwdHs: PST 2SG injunctive with mē

english: The mother was sitting. She was stretching wool and working. She made a garment for her daughter. The daughter put on the garment. In winter she did not get cold.
uncertain: swéh₂s: fem GEN/ABL.SG of the reflexive possessive; does not agree in case with dʰugh₂tréy (DAT)
woséyeto: MID 'clothed herself (in)'
misfit: swéh₂s: GEN/ABL.SG fem, but it modifies dʰugh₂tréy DAT.SG 'for her (own) daughter' (DAT form expected)

english: Son, hear my word. Cut down an oak and carve a bow from it. Take sinew and stretch it on the bow. Do not split the bow. Let them draw it(?). He who has a good bow does not fear the wolf.
uncertain: dukéntu: IMP 3PL 'let them draw it' — no 3PL referent; the addressee is the son (2SG)
h₁yósmōy ... h₁ésti: dative of possession 'to whom is' = 'who has'
bʰinéds: PST 2SG injunctive with mē = prohibitive
dedwóye: PRF 'fears'
misfit: dukéntu: 3PL imperative 'let them draw' amid 2SG instructions to the son; 2SG imperative expected
